correctness.rationale: From the actual eight Git blobs the canonical Pythagorean mate a_c=(1+sqrt(1-c²))(1-qz)/2 and phi=b/a=sqrt(q)(1+z)/(1-qz) give the finite coefficient-sum Gram identity; the reflected AR(1) closed form and q=1 limit follow. For lower bidiagonal D with -q subdiagonal, D G D^*=diag(1+q,(1+q)²,...), so det=(1+q)^(2n+1) and the tridiagonal inverse has the stated boundary entries. Canonical norm gives λmin≥1; an alternating interior vector yields inverse Rayleigh ≥1−1/[2(n−1)], hence uniform λmin→1. If n(1−q_n)→τ, uniform step-kernel convergence to 4 times the Dirichlet–Robin Green kernel implies all fixed-index λ_j(G_n)/n² limits with roots omega cos omega+τ sin omega=0, including τ=0. For n(1−q_n)→∞, Hardy multiplier norm gives λmax≤((1+q)/(1−q))²; a last-half constant vector controls the finite-block Toeplitz defect and reflected correction, giving matching asymptotics. The q→0 small-symbol case and q=1 endpoint do not invalidate the bounds. These are analytic arguments; independent finite checks only corroborate their algebra/numerics.
residual_risks: Continuum Green-eigenvalue theorem is classical, but the claimed finite-section joint-limit transfer is directly justified by uniform step-kernel convergence.
Verification is analytical/numerical independent review, not machine-formal Lean or an external expert attestation.

value.rationale: The canonical monomial basis of H(b_c) is a natural computationally important Hilbert-space sequence, with a concrete conditioning obstruction as the Schur symbol approaches the boundary. It is not an arbitrary finite table: the degree-vs-parameter scaling 1−c_n²≈n⁻² is a sharp phase boundary; the result yields sharp constants, all fixed-index upper eigenvalue limits, and a uniform small-eigenvalue estimate. These quantitative spectral facts have plausible utility for stable polynomial approximation and regularization. The Dirichlet–Robin eigenproblem and AR(1) calculations are known tools, and significance rests specifically on the nontrivial canonical-space crossover, not on renaming an OU eigenvalue formula.
residual_risks: The application is deliberately restricted to the one-parameter real linear Schur-symbol family; no general polynomial-symbol assertion follows.
Continuum Robin equation is preexisting; new value depends on verified original finite-section model-specific synthesis.

limitations: All fixed-index spectral limits are for each fixed j, not uniform in j; the model is only the real linear b_c(z)=c(1+z)/2 family.
Exact OU Dirichlet–Robin continuum eigenvalue law pre-dates this finding; model-specific finite-section identification/crossover remains the assessed contribution.
Results are not externally formally verified, nor are primary literature searches exhaustive.
